To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a testosterone-conjugating activity was present in the cytosolic fraction of human liver, that it was not sedimented by centrifugal force and that it was not separated from an oestriol-glucuronytransferase by chromatography on a Sephadex G200 column.
testosterone and oestradiol are conjugated in the cytosolic fraction of human liver by two different glucuronyl-transferases, one of them being a 17beta-hormone-specific glucuronyl transferase.
testosterone 17beta- glucuronyl-transferase is present in the cytosolic fraction of human liver and that it conjugates the 3alpha-, 3beta-, 16alpha- and 17beta-hy-droxyl groups of oestriols.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the isolation and characterization of a testosterone-conjugating activity from the cytosolic fraction of human liver, which is capable of conjugating the 17beta- as well as the 16alpha- hydroxyl group of steroids.
the purification and characterization of a testosterone glucuronlytransferase (TGT) from the cytosolic fraction of human liver (H-L).
the study of the metabolism of oestriols, and particularly with the formation of the oestriols glucuronides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the testosterone-conjugation and the oestrogen-conjugation activities are catalysed by the same enzyme, testosterone 17 beta-glucuronyltransferase.

the enzyme studied is a glucuronosyltransferase that conjugates the hydroxyl group of the 17beta-position in testosterone and the 16alpha-position in oestriol to yield the corresponding 17beta-glutcuronides and 16alpha-glucuronides respectively.
the testosterone-conjugated enzyme and the oestrogen-conjugating enzyme are identical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have purified a glucuronyl-transferase that conjugates testosterone to its 17beta-holglucuronide.
we have purified a glucuronyl transferase that conjugates testosterone and oestrogen at the 17 beta position.
testosterone and oestrone are conjugated by an enzyme that is present in the cytoplasm of liver cells, and that oestriol is conjugated by an additional enzyme that may be located in the microsomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the testosterone glucuronidation reaction is a very important reaction in the body and that it is a good indicator of liver health.
the enzyme that glucuronidates the 17 beta-OH group of testosterone is different from that conjugating the 16 alpha-OH group of oestiol in the cytosolic fraction of human liver.
the enzyme that conjugates testosterone is different from that conjugating oestriol.
